Going out at night or being outside after dark
Any form of physical contact with others

Memory.value: I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

vignette: Kofi had always been driven to make a difference in his community. As a young detective, he took pride in his work, often going above and beyond to solve cases and bring justice to victims' families. But everything changed one fateful night when Kofi was taken captive by a group of armed assailants while working undercover. For hours, he was held at gunpoint, subjected to verbal abuse and physical intimidation. The memory of that night still lingered, though Kofi struggled to put it into words. He knew what had happened, but the details seemed to get stuck in his throat, refusing to be spoken aloud. When memories did surface, they often came with a jarring soundtrack – the sound of gunfire, the taunts of his captors, the rustling of fabric as he was bound and gagged. Kofi's mind would replay these auditory snippets like a broken record, transporting him back to that terrifying night. In an attempt to regain control, Kofi developed a few coping strategies. He tried hard not to think about the trauma, pushing it to the farthest recesses of his mind whenever memories threatened to resurface. Avoiding nighttime activities became second nature – no more evening patrols or late-night drives home from work. The darkness outside seemed to amplify the shadows within him, making him feel vulnerable and exposed. Kofi's relationships also began to suffer as he struggled with physical contact. His girlfriend, Nia, would try to hold his hand or give him a gentle hug, only to be met with stiff resistance. Kofi knew it wasn't rational – Nia was the one person who had been there for him throughout this ordeal – but any form of touch seemed to trigger an overwhelming sense of unease. As time passed, these avoidance behaviors took their toll on Kofi's daily life. His job performance began to slip; he found himself hesitating at critical moments during investigations or freezing up in high-pressure situations. Nia grew increasingly concerned about his withdrawal from social activities and his growing emotional distance. Their conversations started to revolve around Kofi's anxiety and fears, rather than shared dreams and aspirations. Despite the strain on their relationship, Nia remained a source of comfort for Kofi – one he was desperate not to lose. But there were moments when the memories overwhelmed him, and emotions would flood in without warning. No clear image or memory would accompany these episodes, just an unshakeable sense of dread that left him gasping for air. Kofi knew something had to change. It was Nia who finally convinced him to seek help, after a particularly brutal episode left him shaken for days. As he sat in the therapist's office, Kofi felt a glimmer of hope – maybe this time, he could find a way to break free from the grip of his memories and learn to live with the shadows that haunted him. What terrified him most was losing himself completely, becoming forever trapped in that dark night when everything had gone so terribly wrong.
